coverage: 21 named characters; conservative explicit names, with reviewed Chettam, Farebrother and Lydgate title rules. No global Will, Mary, Garth, Vincy or generic Vicar binding.
chapterNumbering: Live units 1–88; paragraph indices are zero-based.

entities.name: Dorothea Brooke
entities.subtitle: An idealistic young woman
entities.body: Eager to devote her life to something worthwhile, Dorothea looks for a purpose larger than the comfortable future expected of her.

snapshots.name: Dorothea Casaubon
snapshots.body: Dorothea has married Edward Casaubon and left for Rome. She hopes to share in his scholarly work.

snapshots.name: Dorothea Ladislaw
snapshots.body: Dorothea, formerly Mrs. Casaubon, is now Mrs. Ladislaw. Rosamond remembers her generosity with lasting gratitude.

entities.name: Celia Brooke
entities.subtitle: Dorothea’s sister
entities.body: Practical and attentive to ordinary pleasures, Celia often sees what her sister’s ideals obscure.

snapshots.name: Celia Chettam
snapshots.body: Celia has married Sir James Chettam. She is the young Lady Chettam; his mother also bears the title Lady Chettam.

entities.name: Edward Casaubon
entities.subtitle: A scholar at Lowick
entities.body: A clergyman absorbed in an ambitious scholarly project, Casaubon hopes to give his work lasting authority.

entities.name: Tertius Lydgate
entities.subtitle: A doctor new to Middlemarch
entities.body: A young surgeon newly arrived in Middlemarch, Lydgate attracts attention for his intelligence and assured manner.

entities.name: Rosamond Vincy
entities.subtitle: A manufacturer’s daughter
entities.body: Accomplished and socially ambitious, Rosamond imagines a future of refinement beyond the limits of her familiar circle.

snapshots.name: Rosamond Lydgate
snapshots.body: Rosamond has married Tertius Lydgate and is now addressed as Mrs. Lydgate. Dorothea visits their home to speak with the doctor.

entities.name: Fred Vincy
entities.subtitle: Rosamond’s brother
entities.body: Affectionate but unreliable, Fred hopes luck and inheritance will spare him difficult decisions about work.

entities.name: Mary Garth
entities.subtitle: A clear-sighted young woman
entities.body: Mary’s wit and self-respect make her unwilling to confuse affection with excuses for bad conduct.

snapshots.body: Mary Garth and Fred Vincy have married and built a happy life together. Fred has become a successful farmer.

entities.name: Caleb Garth
entities.subtitle: An estate manager
entities.body: Caleb values skilled work and honest dealings. His devotion to useful labor offers a different measure of success from money or status.

entities.name: Will Ladislaw
entities.subtitle: Casaubon’s young relative
entities.body: Casaubon introduces Will as his cousin. The young man is interested in drawing and reluctant to accept other people’s judgments of his abilities.

entities.name: Nicholas Bulstrode
entities.subtitle: A banker and religious patron
entities.body: Bulstrode’s wealth supports local institutions, giving his religious convictions considerable public influence.

entities.name: Harriet Bulstrode
entities.subtitle: Bulstrode’s wife
entities.body: Born into the Vincy family, Harriet combines social pride with warmth and loyalty.

entities.name: Camden Farebrother
entities.subtitle: A clergyman
entities.body: Humane and alert to his own weaknesses, Farebrother offers friendship without demanding that people be flawless.

entities.name: Sir James Chettam
entities.subtitle: A neighboring landowner
entities.body: Well-meaning and attentive to practical improvements, Sir James takes an active interest in the Brooke sisters.

entities.name: John Raffles
entities.subtitle: A visitor at Stone Court
entities.body: A talkative visitor at Stone Court, Raffles affects familiarity and jokes about his own cleverness.

snapshots.body: Raffles is Joshua Rigg’s stepfather. Rigg recalls his cruelty and refuses him further access to Stone Court.
Raffles, Joshua Rigg’s stepfather, also knows Bulstrode from dealings more than twenty years earlier. The banker resents his familiarity and wants to limit their renewed contact.

entities.name: Peter Featherstone
entities.subtitle: A wealthy elderly landowner
entities.body: An elderly property owner whose relations and dependents watch his intentions closely.

entities.name: Mr. Brooke
entities.subtitle: The Brooke sisters’ uncle
entities.body: Dorothea and Celia’s uncle, a landowner with wide interests and uncertain follow-through.

entities.name: Susan Garth
entities.subtitle: Caleb Garth’s wife
entities.body: Caleb’s wife, whose practical judgment supports their household.

entities.name: Mr. Vincy
entities.subtitle: Middlemarch’s mayor
entities.body: A prosperous manufacturer, Mr. Vincy enjoys good company and speaks readily about his own comfort.

entities.name: Mrs. Vincy
entities.subtitle: Mistress of the Vincy household
entities.body: Mrs. Vincy takes pride in her children and the comforts of a prosperous Middlemarch household.

entities.name: Lady Chettam
entities.subtitle: Sir James’s mother
entities.body: Lady Chettam values social standing and takes a lively interest in matters of health.

entities.name: Joshua Rigg
entities.subtitle: A reserved stranger
entities.body: Rigg is a quiet man whose unfamiliar face draws attention among Featherstone’s relations.

snapshots.body: Joshua Rigg is Raffles’s stepson. He provides an allowance for his mother but refuses to support the man who mistreated them.
